questions: Why did the authors combine LSTM and Transformer instead of using only one model?
Do the six selected features — NASDAQ, S&P 500, silver futures, USD/CNY, China bond yield, and coal ETF — really make sense for predicting gold futures?
Can the hybrid model truly handle sudden market shocks like war, rate hikes, or banking crises, or does it only learn past patterns?
The hybrid model performs well, but it is more complex and slower. Is the extra accuracy worth the extra computation cost?
Is prediction accuracy enough, or should the paper also prove that the model helps investors with real trading, hedging, or risk management decisions?
If the model works for Shanghai gold futures, can it also predict Indian gold prices or COMEX gold prices?
The paper says traditional models like ARIMA, GARCH, and VAR are limited for gold futures forecasting. Do the authors explain this limitation clearly enough?
The authors use XGBoost–SHAP to select key features. Is this a strong method for feature selection, or could it still miss important market variables?
